speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head M of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Every year, the Committee would scrutinise the findings listed in the Auditor-General's report.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For example, lapses in procurement and contract management, weaknesses in information technology (IT) controls and gaps in management of grant programmes.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Can I ask the Minister on the role that the Ministry of Finance (MOF) plays in ensuring good governance and accountability within the Public Service?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: How does MOF ensure that value-for-money practices and culture are strongly embedded in the Public Service?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Also, does the Public Service track and measure the effectiveness of Government spending for better decision-making?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The accumulated surpluses in the last four years for this term of Government gave the Finance Minister the fiscal firepower and the critical resources to decisively respond to the virus outbreak and help businesses and Singaporeans that are impacted by the crisis in a timely way.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We have very ambitious spending programmes and plans in the decade ahead, including big-ticket infrastructural items like the Cross Island Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) line, Terminal 5, the ramp-up in healthcare infrastructure, climate change adaptation projects and so on.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: How do we ensure that the Government will spend carefully and prudently on these mega items?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Given its complexity where the projects may cut across Ministries and agency lines, how would the Government ensure that there will be no overlapping of efforts and costs?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Are there clear working protocols established to streamline and harmonise the whole-of-Government efforts here?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mr Chairman, fiscal sustainability and accountability and the use of public funds are important.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, good financial stewardship is essential for Singapore for the years ahead, given the more challenging environment we have for many years down the road.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: These are all major projects that will be implemented over a number of years.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How are we ensuring that the Government spends prudently and appropriately on big-ticket infrastructure and IT projects such that our financial stewardship would be put in good stead, going forward?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Mr Chairman, with the anticipated rise in expenditure, it is important that the Government ensure fiscal sustainability and accountability.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Singapore's strong financials have been instrumental in enabling the country to carry out audacious development projects, as Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat said just now.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, what is the scope, within our budgetary mechanisms, to ensure this trajectory and to ensure inter-generational equity, balancing the needs of current and future generations, especially for big-ticket items like infrastructure and climate change?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Most fundamentally, a healthy and growing economy will be crucial to ensuring a healthy revenue stream.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The Government has also allocated a significant share of the Budget to research and development (R&D) and Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) investments.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: What has the impact of investments in R&D been in elevating and positioning Singapore for the future and in supporting industry transformation?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: They should be expected to practise prudence in their spending and seek the best value for the money they put into their projects.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: How does MOF ensure value-for-money is the responsibility of every Ministry and every public officer?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: What mechanisms are in place to ensure budgets are efficiently and effectively allocated, and to what extent can the whole-of-Government approach be used to explore cost synergies and cross-agency collaboration, in order to avoid duplication of effort and cost?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The reply was that these matters are to be dealt with by Temasek's Board and the Government does not interfere because Temasek operates as a commercial entity.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In 2019, my Parliamentary colleague Mr Png Eng Huat asked about whether remuneration bands can be disclosed for senior officers in sovereign wealth funds (SWFs).

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The reason this is problematic is that the two entities are not privately-held commercial entities in which case the stance would be understandable, but public ones managing public funds.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A 2018 study found that close to 70% of Singapore-listed companies did so.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Singapore Exchange (SGX) and most of the exchanges do not take the view that the disclosure of such information is unnecessary in the public, and shareholders only need to know past financial performance and nothing else, because such disclosure has a bearing on likely future performance and risks, among other reasons.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: SGX Regulation Chief Executive Tan Boon Gin said, and I quote, "Shareholders, especially minorities, deserve to know why company directors and executives are paid the way they are." "The Board and Management, therefore, owe it to investors to explain the link between performance and remuneration." The same reasoning would apply to our SWFs because the Government is the shareholder, the people of Singapore are, by implication, stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In the case of the Norwegian SWF, the government questioned the rising operating expenses of the SWF publicly.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The compensation of the CEO and Chief Information Officer (CIO) of the Norwegian fund are publicly known.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In passing, let me note that I am not holding up the Norway model as one we should emulate in all respects.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am also not calling for Government interference in the commercial operations of the SWFs.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, one of the key trends shaping Singapore's future is the rapid advancement of technology. artificial intelligence (AI), fifth-generation (5G) high-speed mobile connectivity, robotics and blockchain and so on, are poised to disrupt existing industries, eliminating jobs and create new ones.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Growth projections for 5G, robotics and blockchain technology applications are similarly breathtaking.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Traditionally, economic development is predominantly the responsibility of the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI), but increasingly, several other Ministries are overseeing vertical domains which are filled with opportunities for innovation, technology applications and industry development.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: For instance, the Ministry of National Development (MND) has deep knowledge of planning a smart and sustainable city, the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) for smart nation, the Ministry of Transport (MOT) for driverless transportation, the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources (MEWR) for clean energy and water solutions, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) for Fin Tech, and the Ministry of Health (MOH) for telemedicine.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: In all these areas, problem-solving will require multidisciplinary knowledge employing the new technologies I just mentioned.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: These Ministries are in a very good position to champion R&D applications and industry development in their respective domain expert areas.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Would MOF, therefore, consider, when allocating budgets to Ministries, set aside a certain percentage of the Budget for Ministries to take on mandatory industry development roles, including technology planning, R&D and enterprise development within their vertical domains?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: After all, building an advanced knowledge economy is a complex task well beyond the expertise of any single Ministry.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MND also stated that "every parent, regardless of their marital status, ought to be treated with respect." Our policies can help end the discrimination.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is time to level the playing field and treat single unweds with respect.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As citizens, they should qualify for the Parenthood Tax Rebates like all other parents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Working Mother's Child Relief rewards families with children who are Singapore Citizens.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why only encourage married women to remain in the workforce after having children?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is strange that we do not want single unwed women to remain in the workforce after having their child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why discriminate, even after MND has stated again that "every parent regardless of their marital status, ought to be treated with respect"?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Let us respect single unwed mothers who look after their children single-handedly and remain in the workforce despite all the difficulties.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Whether it is the case of a failed marriage or the untimely death of a spouse, the burden and responsibility of single parenthood is a long and arduous journey to undertake.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I have seen a number of single parents at my Meet-the-People sessions over the years.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: While most of them were women, there were single fathers who came along with the children in tow.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The story they share about raising their children all by themselves is a story of love and perseverance.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: A story that highlights the need and importance to have a support network comprising their extended family, friends and even enacted policies to make single parenthood work for them.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Recently, a single father wrote to me to share his experience about raising his two young children.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: While he works hard to put bread on the table for his young family and to provide for his aged parents, he found out that the taxman does not really recognise his role and effort as a single father.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: While this single father can work out the apportionment of the Qualifying Child Relief with his ex-spouse, there is no levy relief for him if he hires a foreign domestic helper to look after his young children.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: This single father would fit the criteria for FML relief to the letter, except for the fact that he is of the wrong gender.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Anyone in his shoes would certainly use whatever that is out there to stretch his hard earned dollar to feed his family.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I hope the Ministry can look into addressing this disparity soon.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: Chairman, Sir, the Public Accounts Committee observed, in its latest report to Parliament, that it is concerned about recurring lapses in procurement and contract management.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: Government agencies were directed to urgently address these recurring lapses and basic mistakes.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: They need to prevent weaknesses from compounding over time, and thus weakening governance and accountability for usage of public funds and resources.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: What training do Government procurement officers undergo, in order to ensure that they are fully conversant with the relevant policies and processes?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: What consequences do the officers-in-charge and management face for lapses in enforcing controls?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: How can the identified lapses be addressed at a whole-of-Government level?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Henry Kwek, you may take both your cuts together.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, the Singapore Government is at the forefront of public policy formulation and implementation.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: It is also one of the largest procurers of goods and services.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Naturally, it constitutes an important demonstration platform and springboard for many companies, especially for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and startups, that want to deliver innovative solutions for Singapore and beyond.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: This is especially so for smart city, climate change and e-services.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: This is especially so, as it is imperative to grow new companies in Singapore for the next phase of our economic development.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Can MOF also share on how we will inform companies of such efforts?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: As the needs of our society grow more diverse and complex, it is inevitable that more regulations are needed to safeguard Singaporeans in different ways.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: At the same time, more regulations mean more processes and greater compliance costs.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: This represents added costs and, potentially, lost productivity to businesses.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I have spoken on this issue on a number of occasions in the past.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I am heartened that over the years, the Government also recognises this issue.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: It has formed the Pro-Enterprise Committee and achieved positive results in cutting red tape.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Can MOF share on how, as part of the Singapore Together movement, MOF and the greater, larger Government agencies can partner businesses on co-creating solutions to reduce compliance costs and streamline processes for greater productivity?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Saktiandi, you may take both cuts together.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Mr Chairman, the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) situation we are facing now has highlighted the importance of digitalisation for work and daily household processes.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Being able to perform many tasks from home has helped to reduce the necessity of gathering and queuing in public places.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: In regular times, digitalisation of existing Public Service processes has brought extensive convenience to citizens and businesses.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Checking our Central Provident Fund (CPF) balances, obtaining information about housing grants, submitting a tender for a public project and so forth have become so easy they can be done from our computers and smartphones.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: How does it engage the older generation who may experience a steep learning curve and may need the necessary devices to benefit from this digitalisation?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: During COVID-19, we saw many heart-warming instances of individuals, organisations and businesses performing acts of kindness, from individuals setting up hand sanitisers for their communities, to businesses giving away masks and organisations persevering with their regular food distributions.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Singaporeans also donated generously to organisations in need.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: It is a reminder of how much we can achieve together.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: How can the Government work together with Singaporeans, stakeholders and partners to ensure that we can inculcate the society and people with empathy, care and strength to overcome challenges?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Chairman, Sir, the number of ground-up initiatives supporting the community and underprivileged have increased over the years.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In part, it was contributed by greater social awareness, corporate social responsibility and more funding channelled to support these causes.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I commend all the immense good efforts and initiatives that everyone across the country has contributed to benefit the different individuals amongst us.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I ask that we do not stop here and continue to do more.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We have been on the journey of promoting digital services.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For a while, the focus had been on our seniors and keeping them abreast of digital application.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As we continue to bring more on board this digital journey, I feel that another group of people who will benefit immensely are people with special needs.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I encourage the community and businesses to use their knowledge, technology, tools and people network to strengthen this partnership in helping people with special needs.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I ask we particularly look at some aspects in their life journey.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For those with special needs, more patience and efforts are even required on their part.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: To assume responsibility in managing their life, they need more intuitive systems and aid.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: With big data, there can be analysis done to provide reference for them on how to do certain things or automate it for them.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: It is not easy for them to get coverage for some basic investment policies, much less medical coverage.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: By precluding them, they are not just financially worse off but it makes it even harder for them to take stewardship of their health in old age.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Further, not all their health issues require hospitalisation.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Planning is of utmost importance and how to do it becomes critical for people with special needs to learn in order to minimise risk and disruption in their lives.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Before investments and housing needs, they could require lessons on financial budgeting around necessities versus good to have, understanding what is genuinely good for their well-being, and prioritising to prevent straining their own resources.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Moving out of the comfort zone in communal setting is not the easiest for many of them.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We should try to break through social stigma at the workplace, community and family, and increasingly integrate them into our society.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Build emotional and relational connections with people of special needs and give them a safe and respected environment to be in.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Members for their questions and comments for MOF.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Members’ cuts cover three broad topics: first, fiscal sustainability and accountability; second, transformation of Public Service processes; and third, enhancing service delivery to be more business- and citizen-centric.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will speak on the first topic, as well as the questions on Reserves and tax matters.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second Minister for Finance Indranee Rajah will cover the other two topics.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are a small country with no natural resources, exposed to global forces beyond our control.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Mr Liang Eng Hwa highlighted just now, our prudent fiscal strategy has provided us with the resources to respond promptly and decisively to crises, and also to continue investing for the future and for the long term.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They were the result of prudent fiscal policies put in place by our pioneering leaders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, it is imperative that we continue to uphold this sound fiscal approach in order to maintain our strong financial position.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, as Ms Foo Mee Har mentioned just now and I think Mr Cedric Foo also said earlier in the Budget Debate, every generation must contribute its fair share and not leave an undue burden for the next generation to bear.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why we must continue to pay for recurrent needs with recurrent revenues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why, every year, when we prepare the Budget, we do not come to Parliament to appropriate monies just for the sake of spending every cent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, we look at each project on its merit, we spend on what we deem to be cost-effective, and then if there are any savings, we set these aside for anticipated future needs, as we did this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We set aside some amount of money for climate change.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Upholding such financial prudence and discipline is a reflection of our commitment to Singaporeans, not just the present generation of Singaporeans but, as Deputy Prime Minister said just now in the Budget round-up speech, it is also a reflection of our commitment to future generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A key part of our prudent fiscal system is to have a resilient and diverse revenue base, as well as to have effective and value-for-money public spending.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I will elaborate on each of these.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Ms Foo Mee Har highlighted, a healthy and growing economy is crucial to sustaining our revenues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why the Government invests upstream to build capabilities of Singaporeans and to provide maximum opportunities for Singaporeans to excel.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is how we can continue to enlarge and grow our economic pie.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Lee Yi Shyan asked whether Ministries play a role in industry development and contributing to economic growth.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While MTI is the lead agency for the economy, various Government agencies do take on sectoral lead roles.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, as all Members would know, MAS oversees the financial services sector; the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) looks at industry development for the IT sector; and the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) takes care of the built environment, and so on.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All in all, we have 23 ITMs and we have set aside budgets for the respective lead agencies to support the implementation of the ITMs that would include technology adoption, R&D and industry development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of this work is coordinated under the Future Economy Council.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To Ms Foo Mee Har’s question on the progress of our investments into economic transformation, we are starting to see these efforts bear fruit.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har also asked about the impact of our R&D investments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The National Research Foundation (NRF) recently completed its mid-term review of the RIE2020 Plan, and this RIE2020 is on track to meeting its outcomes, such as in supporting industry growth and catalysing greater innovative activities in the private sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In less than two years, RIE2020 has also exceeded the target of supporting more than 250 successful startups.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we are seeing positive results, but there is always room to do better.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And all Government agencies are fully aware that they must continue to achieve maximum value from the public funds they are entrusted with, so as to keep transforming our industries and sustaining economic growth.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Just as we want to grow our revenues, it is equally important to ensure that our spending is prudent, efficient and cost-effective.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har asked about the Budget mechanisms in place to manage expenditure growth and to incentivise public officers to achieve savings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our Block Budget Framework sets a spending cap for Ministries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Within this Block Budget Framework, if Ministries have any savings, they can roll over part of the savings from the operating budget to the next financial year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For big-ticket items, such as infrastructure and infocomm technology (ICT) projects, which Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Liang Eng Hwa spoke about, MOF applies additional scrutiny to evaluate such projects for their worthiness and cost-effectiveness before embarking on them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Large infrastructure projects, like the coastal protection infrastructure that Mr Saktiandi Supaat mentioned, would be reviewed by a panel of technical experts from the private and public sector and academia, before they are given the go-ahead.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Take the Cross Island Line (CRL), for example.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The depot for CRL at Changi East was initially planned to be underground to optimise above-ground land use.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: After working with the Land Transport Authority (LTA) and agencies to evaluate the costs and benefits of this approach, agencies found a way to site the depot above ground with reduced engineering risks and at lower cost.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For issues that may not fall neatly within a specific agency’s domain or area of responsibility, we agree with Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Liang Eng Hwa that agencies do need to collaborate to avoid duplication of efforts and costs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To facilitate this, MOF has set up joint programme budgets for cross-cutting areas, like ICT and Smart Systems, cybersecurity and RIE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, the cybersecurity programme budget was put in place by MOF, Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) and Smart Nation and Digital Government Office (SNDGO) to improve coordination, discipline and prioritisation for the build-up of whole-of-Government cybersecurity programmes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, this sort of partnership helps the Government to make more informed and robust resourcing decisions as a whole.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MOF will continue to identify areas that warrant such multi-Ministry or multi-agency approaches and set aside joint programme budgets, where necessary, to get agencies to work together for more effective outcomes, rather than to do so in their individual agency silos.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ultimately, while budgeting mechanisms can facilitate discipline in the way we use public monies, the best way to ensure prudence and effectiveness is to instil a value-for-money (VFM) mindset in every public officer, as Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Liang Eng Hwa rightly highlighted.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Again, this is a continual work in progress, but we have seen improvements over the years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It sets outcome-based KPIs, such as percentage of commuters' journeys completed within 45 minutes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, there are clear outcomes for its spending.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MOT also conducts VFM workshops for its officers to share ideas and best practices, and has its very own Ministry’s VFM Awards for projects that generate significant dollar savings and benefits for citizens.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A key part of ensuring every dollar has been well-spent is tracking and evaluating the effectiveness of our spending, and we do so by setting KPIs upfront during policy design so that spending is tied to the desired outcomes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Then, we review the policies regularly to ensure that they are on track to fulfil the outcomes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) started this as a pilot in 2016 targeting to benefit about 1,000 children, with carefully designed indicators and a clear evaluation plan.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since then, the team has been monitoring outcomes, such as child developmental milestones, preschool attendance and quality of parent-child interactions, to assess the programme's effectiveness.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Thereafter, we will take stock again to see how we can expand KidSTART further.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, this example illustrates the approach we take, how we scale up progressively, relying on data, evidence and learning points to improve the programme, and then, constantly review the effectiveness of public spending.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa earlier shared about his work as a Member of PAC.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Addressing lapses that Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Ms Foo Mee Har mentioned is a continuing effort that requires balance between controls and efficiency.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Like any large organisation, we recognise that it will not be possible to achieve zero lapses, given the high volume of transactions across the Government.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Nevertheless, where lapses are found, our agencies will take immediate steps to address them and strengthen their controls to minimise recurrence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This may include relooking at our policies, practices and systems, as well as stepping up training of public officers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I assure Ms Foo Mee Har that the Government adopts a zero-tolerance approach to fraud and corruption.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Those who commit wrongdoing will face the full measure of the law.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Where appropriate, disciplinary actions are also brought against officers responsible for lapses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MOF will spare no efforts as we work with agencies to ensure that the Government remains responsible, open and accountable in our use of public funds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to strengthen our system of checks and balances and instil discipline in every officer to make sound spending decisions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Next, Mr Leon Perera asked about succession plans and disclosure practices of SWFs, particularly of the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation (GIC) and Temasek.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government has explained its position clearly on these issues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The two entities put out a lot of information every year in their annual reports, highlighting not just their performance, but also extensive information and commentary on their investment approach and their outlook.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, over the years, GIC and Temasek have progressively put out a lot more information than they used to.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to encourage the two entities to review and examine what additional information they would like to put out in their annual reports.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: From the Government's point of view, our key consideration is this: whatever disclosure requirements that the two entities put out should be part of an overall system that enables these two entities to maximise their ability to secure long-term returns for the benefit of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to have a system that allows our two entities to succeed in achieving their mandate and we have to be very mindful of what kind of disclosure requirements we place on them, and be careful of not leading them to pursue indicators that can lead to undesirable behaviours.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, if we were to insist, as some have suggested before, on publishing annual indicators of performance, some of these entities may then be driven towards short-term performance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That would not be in our interest because these are entities that are looking at achieving long-term financial returns.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we are insistent on them disclosing indicators of fees and expenses to a great level of detail, it may lead these entities towards minimising expenses, potentially eroding capabilities or diminishing their talent pool, which would also not be in our interest.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we are quite careful and deliberate in thinking about what sort of system we want to put in place and, ultimately, it is a system that enhances the performance of the two entities in securing long-term returns.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why if Members look at what is published, it is the long-term returns, net of all expenses incurred, and the information is published for both GIC and Temasek in their annual reports.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ultimately, we want to preserve the competitive advantage of our two investment entities vis-a-vis other market players and we want to maximise their ability to secure long-term returns for the benefit of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Png Eng Huat suggested extending existing tax reliefs to unwed parents and single fathers respectively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Again, let me explain the Government's considerations here.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this way, we support all parents, including unwed parents, to give their children education opportunities, good healthcare and a conducive social environment, so they can realise their fullest potential in life.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, for the Foreign Maid Levy Relief, this was specifically granted to encourage married women to continue working.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, there were specific objectives tied to these schemes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Having said that, all Members would know that our schemes are never cast in stone.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We continue to review and recalibrate them from time to time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Members will recall that we have reviewed and extended support to unwed parents in recent years, including the CDA benefits as well as the full 16 weeks of Government-paid maternity leave.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These things will continue to progress and evolve.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I would encourage Members also to consider this.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides looking at specific tax reliefs and comparing the benefits for one group versus another, it is important to take a step back and look at the broader picture.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to give every child a good start in life, provide support for all parents and build strong families in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have different schemes and policy tools to achieve these multiple objectives and we will continue to finetune and review our schemes to achieve the optimal balance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Chairman, MOF is committed to ensuring that our spending is effective and sustainable over the long term and we will do so in partnership with the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will let Second Minister for Finance Indranee Rajah address the other questions raised.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, I will now address Members' questions which fall under two broad topics: first, how the Government is transforming Public Service processes to better serve our people; and second, how we are enhancing service delivery to be more business- and citizen-centric.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Minister Chan Chun Sing spoke earlier about transforming the Public Service for the future.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I will cover MOF's efforts in transforming Government procurement through rule reviews and the pervasive use of technology.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This contributes to being more nimble, innovative and effective, as urged by Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Ms Foo Mee Har.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, MOF has used regulatory sandboxes to lift procurement rules and allow agencies to test new approaches.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One such sandbox enables Government agencies to negotiate with the most qualified bidders in open tenders to identify alternative solutions that provide better value for the Government.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, we are introducing more dynamism in some of our bulk contracts to be responsive to market changes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While current ICT bulk contracts allow suppliers to refresh their prices, we are introducing further dynamism by allowing new requirements and new suppliers to be added throughout a multi-year contract.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is especially pertinent in an environment of rapid technology changes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Suppliers will be able to offer new products and services to the Government, without waiting for bulk contracts to expire.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, public officers can soon make small value purchases directly from e-commerce sites, which will enhance speed and convenience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, the Public Service spends more than $60 million annually on small value items, such as pantry supplies, stationery and small electrical appliances.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: By the end of this year, MOF and the Government Technology Agency (GovTech) will enable public officers to make small value purchases from e-commerce sites seamlessly, without having to claim reimbursement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A fully automated e-commerce model will lighten the processing workload on our corporate staff.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are partnering our vendors in this digitalisation journey, particularly our SMEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: By bringing their businesses online, SMEs can digitalise their processes from order to invoice to payment and improve productivity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: SMEs can access an additional channel to supply Government agencies and other buyers and expand their reach beyond Singapore's shores.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked how we are enhancing the Government procurement approach to enable SMEs and startups to develop innovative solutions and help them grow.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to look at how we can facilitate their participation and support their growth.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Henry Kwek also asked how we inform companies of such efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One key way is to partner our Trade Associations and Chambers to reach out to them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For instance, MOF regularly engages the Singapore Business Federation to gather feedback from their members and provide clarifications on Government procurement matters.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: GovTech, as the Government’s lead for ICT procurement, has regular platforms with SGTech to facilitate collaborations with the tech industry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One of the initiatives shared with SGTech is IMDA's Open Innovation Platform (OIP), which enables smaller enterprises to better access Government opportunities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This attracted 191 proposals, with more than 90% coming from SMEs, startups and individuals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The National Environment Agency (NEA), for example, has posted a challenge on addressing air pollution from vehicles' smoke emission.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: NEA is now working with the awarded startup to co-develop a proof-of-concept where video analytics capabilities will be used to detect smoke emissions remotely yet accurately.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If the solution proves to be effective, it can be piloted and scaled up without the need for further tenders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For the ICT sector, we have gone a step further to list promising Singapore-based tech startups in a panel for Government agencies to consider first.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The SG:D Spark programme gives these startups priority access to Government projects to build capabilities and track record for further growth.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Impress.ai is a local SME on the SG:D Spark programme which helps companies automate their recruitment process using AI.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It has grown its clientele to 10 Government agencies in its two years on the programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These agencies, in turn, have benefited from a more efficient and effective recruitment process.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, Ngee Ann Polytechnic reduced the time taken to review over 4,000 applications, from 470 hours to just two hours.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked how MOF has tapped on digitalisation to enhance its interactions with businesses and citizens.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Henry Kwek also talked about reducing business compliance costs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Earlier this year, the Accountant-General’s Department announced that the Government has taken the lead to adopt the Nationwide e-Invoicing Network.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This provides our 20,000 vendors currently on e-invoicing arrangements with an additional channel to transmit invoices from their accounting systems to the Government.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Being on the network also allows vendors to exchange documents seamlessly with one another, including overseas counterparties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will make it easier, more convenient and less costly to transact with the Government.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Within the Public Service, we have conducted reviews to digitalise processes and do away with signatures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Where signatures are still required, electronic signatures will be the norm.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have gone one step further to integrate digital solutions across platforms and agencies to create seamless digital touchpoints.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In partnership with software providers, the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA) and Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) are enabling seamless filing for smaller companies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Using source data from accounting records, financial and tax returns can now be automatically generated and submitted directly to ACRA and IRAS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Even as we seek to create seamless digital touchpoints with citizens, we must also help those who might require more customised assistance, as Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Miss Cheryl Chan highlighted.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IRAS has been working with taxi and private hire car (PHC) drivers on a chat-filing initiative to simplify tax filing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Through this collaboration, IRAS developed a conversational-style form to help drivers understand the information they need to report.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We recognise that the Government does not have a monopoly of ideas or resources.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For Singapore to succeed, we must harness the collective wisdom and ideas of our people.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I am glad that Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Miss Cheryl Chan highlighted the SG Together movement, which will anchor our nation-building going forward.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Budget 2020 is a good example of SG Together in action.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We engaged and received suggestions from about 6,000 contributors, almost 40% more than last year's Budget.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to step up our engagement efforts so that all Singaporeans can have a say in our Budget.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Beyond engagement, we seek to actively partner our businesses, community groups and citizens to create policy solutions together.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Take, for example, the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme under Budget 2020.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This had its origins in early discussions between the Tsao Foundation and the Government.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Tsao Foundation did a pilot study to provide dollar-matching on CPF savings for a small group of older women.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We then scaled up the idea into a nation-wide programme to boost the retirement adequacy of eligible lower- and middle-income seniors with little retirement savings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also leveraged data sharing via Application Programming Interface (API) exchanges and crowdsourcing through hackathons to co-create solutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For instance, IRAS' API Marketplace and ACRA's API Mall allow developers and businesses to harness data and create applications that interface seamlessly with Government systems.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These APIs are currently used by over 150 organisations to develop business and productivity solutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have also taken a further step to partner businesses and empower the community to co-implement solutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, our banks and telecommunication service providers are valuable partners under IMDA and Enterprise Singapore's Start Digital initiative, who help introduce business solutions through their touchpoints with SMEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also leveraged partnerships to promote inclusive growth, and foster a caring and resilient society, which Miss Cheryl Chan spoke about.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Tote Board's Enabling Lives Initiative, managed by SG Enable and the National Council of Social Service, is one example of how various stakeholders, such as social service agencies, academia and corporates, work together to deliver projects that improve the well-being of persons with disabilities and caregivers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Miss Cheryl Chan mentioned, people with special needs will benefit immensely from the use of digital tools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under Tote Board's initiative, a social enterprise called Digital D.R.E.A.M. pioneered the use of virtual reality systems to provide immersive learning opportunities for students with special needs, such as learning about road safety in a safe environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Digital D.R.E.A.M. has since partnered various Special Education schools to develop tailored content materials for their students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Later this year, Tote Board will launch the second tranche of the initiative.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We look forward to more collaborations with our community partners to deliver impactful and innovative solutions in various aspects, such as lifeskills and assistive technology, for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: More details will be shared at MSF's COS debate later.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: We have MND saying that every mother and every father is equal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Second, with these two rebate and relief, there are single parents who qualify for it, who are the divorcees.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, why can we not just extend it to the single unweds, unless, of course, we are saying we want that as a form of deterrent so that people do not have children out of wedlock?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: We are not fighting for the money here.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: We are fighting the stigma and the discrimination.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And I know MOF will support this as this is a Unity Budget.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Chairman, I think Mr Louis Ng is talking about the support for single unwed parents in the context of MND's issues on housing; and certainly, if I were to wear my MND hat, we have said that we want to provide housing even for single unwed parents in the interest of the child.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But the question here is a different one.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think the question here is: do we want to provide support for parenthood in the context of marriage?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But it does not mean that we are not supporting children.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I said, schemes that provide support for children, we will ensure that the children have them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It does not mean that we are not supporting parents, whether you are a single father, a single mother or whether you are a divorcee.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But so long as we take the view that we want to provide support for parenthood in the context of marriage, that gradient will exist.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Do we not want the gradient and treat all as equal?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is a continuing journey, as I alluded to earlier.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think in this House, we have heard calls for more support for parenthood in the context of marriage, too.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, obviously, there are different views and we will have to manage these different views and continue to refine and improve our schemes over time to manage this diversity of views and to address the different objectives, as I highlighted earlier.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, can I ask the Minister if this continued growth in NIRC is realistic, sustainable, given the grimmer outlook now, not just because of the current COVID-19 fallout but also of more concern are the longer-term global structural stresses that we saw and the persistent near-zero interest rate environment that is still there?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Can we expect this NIRC to grow to fund our Budget in the future?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As Mr Liang Eng Hwa is fully aware, NIRC is tied to the long-term expected returns of our investment entities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, the critical words are "long-term expected returns".

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not impacted by immediate market volatilities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we are not so concerned about that.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But looking ahead, looking at the long term, there are, indeed, reasons for concerns.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we do expect more pressures in the longer-term investment environment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, geopolitical tensions will be a long-term issue between America and China.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That contestation for power will be with us for quite a while and it may lead to a more bifurcated world over a period of time.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will likely see more nationalist and protectionist pressures continuing, which means that the pace of globalisation will slow.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We may even get deglobalisation, which will cause global growth to be lower for longer periods of time.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In developed markets, we see ageing populations, lower productivity, stagnating growth.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do not assume that our NIRC will always be able to keep pace with our spending needs and that is why all the more we must not take our current fiscal strength for granted.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I hope the Minister will agree with me that it is not a deterrence.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Not providing single unweds with the Parenthood Tax Rebate and Working Mother's Child Relief is not a deterrence.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And I also hope that the Minister will agree with me that it is not an incentive.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It might be this worry that if we provide the single unweds with more benefits, all of a sudden, there is going to be a huge population of children born out of wedlock.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I do not think that will happen as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And if we do not think that it is going to incentivise or discourage, then again, what is stopping us from levelling this playing field and ending the discrimination?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Chairman, I respect Mr Louis Ng's views.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think there are many in this House who will feel like that.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are many who will also ask for additional support for parenthood in the context of marriage, as has been the case before.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, like I said, there will be a range of perspectives on this matter.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We take all this into consideration in continuing to review and update our schemes.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: I actually would like to continue the clarification started by Member Liang Eng Hwa and the Minister's eloquent reply.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: I noted the same strong growth projected for 2020.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: And I do understand we project long-term expected returns.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: To me, that is a very big achievement and we are very grateful, because we can then use it to fund our Budget.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: But then, what would the trend be in terms of percentage increases, or 9.3% this year versus last year, right?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: In wealth management, if you can achieve 9.3% for long-term expected growth, that would be an amazing achievement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, the base changes, too, in order to get your NIRC.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have a rigorous process to go through what that rate of return should be.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: MOF will review it as well, and then we put it up to the Council of Presidential Advisers and the President finally has to approve the figures.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have explained the process, it is a rigorous process that goes through quite a bit of scrutiny before we finalise the figure.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The trends which I talked about earlier, what Mr Liang Eng Hwa had asked for, are concerns that we have, looking ahead.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we are mindful and we are watchful over this.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Mr Chairman, I did not file a cut for this Head, but if there are questions, I am prepared to give way.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I am assuming that there is no one behind me who has raised his or her hand.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: If it is fine, I will just proceed to ask my question.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I am going to ask a question but I did not speak during for this Head, Mr Chairman, so I feel that those who had filed cuts should have first priority.

speaker: The Chairman
text: If you can couch it as a clarification, I will allow it.

speaker: The Chairman
text: If it is a new question, I will not allow it.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I will put the clarification to Minister Lawrence Wong following up on the question on NIRC.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I remember when we had the debate in this House in July 2015 on the amendment to the Constitution, we confirmed that the formula that was derived, the figures the NIRC reflects is very conservative.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Even more so when the broader economic environment is poor.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I confirm then that the prospects of a "famine and feast" of NIRC, as a budget line item, actually is very, very minimal?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The second clarification is pertaining to the question I had put in my Budget speech about the formula that the Government was proceeding with insofar as debt financing was concerned and the implications that has on some sort of fiscal room in subsequent Budgets.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Is there any clarity on that particular point, because the repayment period is stretched, instead of a lumpy one-time or two-time payment?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Technically, the second question is a new question not a clarification, but I will answer it anyway.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, it is not tied to immediate short-term market performance.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Conversely, if it is a bonanza year and markets were to go up, it does not impact on our NIRC because we are looking at expected long-term returns.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, to the first point, it is not so much a conservative element.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is simply that we look at a long-term figure in order to derive the NIRC.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do not look at short-term market changes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, that is our focus for deriving the NIRC.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And that is also why we have continually emphasised that we hold our investment entities to the performance measure of their long-term returns, rather than looking at year-to-year performance.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Because year-to-year performance can vary, depending on the market, but we look at long-term trends.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: MOF will reveal the details of the debt financing arrangement in due course.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Rather than to fund this entirely from the Budget, we will do it through borrowing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We think this is a more equitable arrangement for major infrastructure that spans a long period of time, then both current and future generations will pay for the payment of that infrastructure through its useful life.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Doing so may provide you some fiscal space in the interim, of course, compared to the alternative of funding everything upfront.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But I think it would also be wrong to assume that this fiscal space can be entirely spent away because you need to pay for it later on anyway.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If you were to spend all of that fiscal space immediately on something that carries a long tail, down the road, you will end up with difficulties paying for the debt repayment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, the idea of borrowing is not so much to provide fiscal space.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is really one where we look at the infrastructure spending we will need to incur going forward, it is likely to be another lump that is coming up in terms of infrastructure needs, like we did when we first financed our first MRT project.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, now, in the new phase of development, there will be major infrastructure projects coming up.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We think it is more equitable that the Government borrow and then spread out the repayment over the lifespan of the project rather than to fund everything upfront, which would then present too much of a burden on the current generation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not so much to provide fiscal relief or fiscal space.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Liang, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: He has not only shown fiscal firepower but also standing power – speaking and standing for more than two hours in both speeches.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: I also want to thank Minister Lawrence Wong and Minister Indranee Rajah for responding to our cuts and also the various engagements that we have with the Government Parliamentary Committee for Finance and Trade and Industry.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: And finally, to the MOF colleagues, they must have worked really hard this time with the fluid circumstances.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: I hope the young officers can now make up for their Valentine's Day that they missed out as the Deputy Prime Minister has mentioned.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: With that, Sir, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
